proposal.comment: [Playbook] TrueLink's indemnity in Section 12.b covers only its own breach of contract, while we give a broad indemnity in 12.a; we need TrueLink, as the party supplying the Interface and hosting, to defend us against third-party IP infringement claims and against its own unlawful conduct, data compromise and gross negligence. If TrueLink prefers, we can accept an IP indemnity with the usual exclusions (our content, modifications and specifications) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies.

ops.newText: claim arising out of (i) any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations or agreements hereunder; (ii) any allegation that the Interface, the Hosting Services, the Support Services or any other software, materials or services provided by TrueLink infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property right; (iii) any breach by TrueLink of any applicable law, rule or regulation; (iv) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content, Credit Data or other Client data caused by TrueLink; or (v) TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct. The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of any claim for which indemnity is sought, and the indemnifying party shall have control of the defense and settlement of such claim (provided that no settlement imposing any obligation or admission on the indemnified party shall be made without its prior written consent), with the reasonable cooperation of the indemnified party at the indemnifying party's expense.
ops.oldText: claim arising out of any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations or agreements hereunder.

proposal.summary: Expand TrueLink's indemnity to cover third-party IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorized disclosure of Client data and gross negligence/willful misconduct.

quote: b. TrueLink shall indemnify and hold Client harmless, its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents and licensors harmless from and against all claims, actions, expenses, losses, and liabilities, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising from or relating to any
rationale: Section 12.b gives us a TrueLink indemnity, but it is limited to TrueLink's breach of the Agreement or failure to perform its obligations; it contains no third-party intellectual property infringement indemnity for the Interface/hosting services, no indemnity for TrueLink's breach of law, no indemnity for unauthorized access to or disclosure of our data, and none for TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct. No IP indemnity appears elsewhere (the only non-infringement covenants run from Client, e.g. §8 on Client Content and §2 on domain names), while §12.a imposes a very broad indemnity on us. Under the playbook the vendor must defend third-party IP claims and its own misconduct, so we expanded §12.b and added standard notice/control/cooperation procedure.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 2(d) confirms TrueLink keeps the Interface, which we accept, but the Agreement never says who owns the Support Services work product or our content, marks and borrower/loan data, and Section 8(d) lets TrueLink exploit Credit Data. We have added a short ownership clause assigning deliverables to us with a perpetual, royalty-free licence to any TrueLink IP embedded in them, confirming we retain our content and data, and excluding joint ownership; if TrueLink prefers to keep title to its generic tools, we can instead take a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables.

ops.text: e. Client Ownership. All results of the Support Services and any other deliverables, work product, materials or modifications prepared by TrueLink for Client under this Agreement (excluding the Interface and TrueLink's Intellectual Property) shall be owned by Client, and TrueLink hereby irrevocably assigns to Client all right, title and interest therein. To the extent any TrueLink Intellectual Property is embedded in or reasonably necessary to use such results, deliverables or work product, TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license to use, modify and sublicense the same for Client's business purposes. As between the parties, Client retains all right, title and interest in and to the Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property and all borrower, loan applicant and customer data submitted through, or stored in connection with, the Interface or the Web Site, and the license granted in Section 8(d) conveys no ownership of any such data to TrueLink. Nothing in this Agreement creates any joint ownership of intellectual property.

proposal.summary: Add Client ownership of Support Services work product, Client Content/IP and borrower data, with licence-back of embedded TrueLink IP and no joint ownership

quote: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
rationale: The only ownership provision (Section 2(d)) addresses TrueLink's retention of the Interface, which is acceptable (vendor keeping its platform). However, the Agreement contains no counterpart provision confirming that we own what we pay for or put in: there is no ownership or assignment language covering the results of the Support Services (Section 4 programmer work product), and although "Client Content" and "Client's Intellectual Property" are defined (p0011, p0012), they are only referenced as confidential information (Sections 8(e), 10(b), 10(c)) and never as our property. Worse, Section 8(d) (p0054) grants TrueLink a worldwide right to "use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit ... and store Credit Data" — i.e., borrower/loan applicant data — with no statement that ownership of that data remains with us. The playbook requires Customer ownership of deliverables with a licence-back of embedded Vendor IP, retention of all rights in Customer Data, and no joint ownership. Added a single ownership clause after Section 2(d) that assigns deliverables/work product to us, licences back any embedded TrueLink IP on a perpetual, royalty-free basis, confirms we retain our content, marks and borrower data (and that the Section 8(d) licence transfers no ownership), and rules out joint ownership. Fallback (licence rather than assignment of generic tools) offered in the comment.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made the liability cap mutual (currently only TrueLink's liability is limited, leaving Client exposed without limit) and set it at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, with a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages. Consistent with our playbook, indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Client's payment obligations are not counted against it; as a fallback we can accept a mutual cap at 12 months' fees with at least those carve-outs.

ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CLIENT UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) USD 1,000,000, AND NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 12, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. CLIENT'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT CONSTITUTE DAMAGES SUBJECT TO, OR COUNT AGAINST, THE FOREGOING CAP.
ops.oldText: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap mutual with a USD 1,000,000 floor, add a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and place confidentiality, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap.

quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.
rationale: The only liability limitation in the agreement (p0077) is one-sided: it caps TrueLink alone, leaving Client's liability wholly uncapped despite Client's broad indemnity in Section 12a. The cap basis is also narrow ("compensation paid", not paid or payable, and no USD floor), and there is no mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and no carve-out framework for confidentiality (Section 10), indemnification, fraud or IP infringement. We redlined p0077 to a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, added a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, defined Excluded Claims as uncapped, and confirmed Client's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a carve-out so that we may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and made TrueLink's assignments subject to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and not to our competitors. Our playbook requires freedom to reorganize or be acquired without vendor consent; if helpful, we can accept a mutual notice-based successor right with consent not unreasonably withheld for other assignments.

ops.newText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed; provided, that no such approval shall be required for (a) an assignment by either party to a financially responsible affiliate or (b) an assignment by Client to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or equity. In no event shall TrueLink assign or transfer this Agreement to a competitor of Client. No change in the ownership or control of Client shall constitute an assignment hereunder or give rise to any right of TrueLink to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.
ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.

proposal.summary: Add successor/M&A carve-out for Client, reasonableness standard, and competitor bar on TrueLink assignments

quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
rationale: Section 15 restricts assignment mutually with only an affiliate carve-out. It falls short of our preferred position in three respects: (i) Client has no carve-out to assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, so an acquisition of Mortgage Logic.com would require TrueLink's consent; (ii) the consent standard is unqualified rather than "not unreasonably withheld"; and (iii) nothing prevents TrueLink from assigning to a Client competitor. No change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists elsewhere in the document (searches for "change of control", "merger" and "successor" returned nothing), so the redline adds a confirmatory statement that a Client ownership change is not a deemed assignment. The redline is a single in-place amendment to Section 15 reaching the preferred position; the mutual notice-based fallback is offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made the credit report sourcing commitment permissive, as our playbook does not accept exclusivity or requirements obligations on the Client. If TrueLink needs volume comfort, we can accept a commitment limited to credit reports for a 12-month term that ends automatically if TrueLink fails to meet the Section 3 performance standards.

ops.newText: Subject to the foregoing, Client may, but shall not be obligated to, order from TrueLink a credit report on any borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface, and nothing in this Agreement shall require Client to purchase credit reports or any other products or services exclusively from TrueLink.
ops.oldText: Subject to the foregoing, Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface.

proposal.summary: Remove requirements-style obligation for Client to order every credit report from TrueLink.

quote: Subject to the foregoing, Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface.
rationale: Section 3(i) imposes a requirements-style exclusivity on us: we must source a credit report from TrueLink for every borrower underwritten through a System using the Interface, with no volume, term or performance-based exit. Although Section 2(a) preserves our general freedom to license or develop competing software and services, it does not cover credit reports, so the sourcing commitment stands as an open-ended sole-supplier obligation on the Client. Playbook preferred position is no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on the Customer, so we made the ordering right permissive and confirmed non-exclusivity; the fallback (credit reports only, 12 months, terminating on failure to meet the Section 3 performance standards) is offered in the comment. The non-exclusive licence in Section 2(a) and the non-exclusive Credit Data licence to TrueLink in Section 8(d) are not deviations.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty, late-fee or early-termination charge payable by Client (our party) appears anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "liquidated", "penalty", "damages", "interest" return no hits, and the only Client payment obligations are ordinary invoiced fees for Hosting and Support Services (§ 5a, § 6). The termination provision (§ 14) lets Client terminate on notice with services simply running to the end of the following month, with no stipulated sum, minimum remaining-term payment or exit fee. The § 5a "not less than $____ per month" floor is a pricing minimum for services actually received during the term, not a stipulated damages amount or termination charge, and the § 12 liability cap runs against TrueLink only. This satisfies the preferred position: no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer, so no redline is required.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the licence to cover Client's affiliates and contractors acting on Client's behalf, since our personnel, group companies and outsourced service providers all need to use the Interface, and we have confirmed the licence and Agreement transfer with the business to a successor in a merger or sale of assets. If broad affiliate coverage is a concern, we can accept affiliates being added on written notice to TrueLink.

ops.newText: TrueLink hereby grants to Client, its affiliates and its contractors acting on Client's behalf a non-exclusive license to use the Interface
ops.oldText: TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface

ops.newText: except no such approval shall be required for an assignment by Client to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or of the business to which this Agreement relates.
ops.oldText: except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.

proposal.summary: Extend licence to Client's affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf, and permit transfer to a successor.

quote: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.
rationale: The grant in § 2(a) runs to "Client" only, with no coverage for Client's affiliates or for contractors acting on Client's behalf, and no notice mechanism to add them, so group companies and outsourced providers cannot lawfully use the Interface. The licence is not revocable at will (§ 2(c) runs until termination of the Agreement), so revocability is acceptable; however § 15 (p0080) permits transfer without consent only to a financially responsible affiliate, leaving a successor in an M&A transaction subject to TrueLink's consent, short of the playbook's transferability position. Redline adds affiliates and contractors to the grant and a successor-transfer carve-out; fallback is affiliates added on written notice.

quote: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restraint binds us. Section 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) contains only compliance, access-control, content and anti-spam covenants, and Section 7 is limited to unsolicited e-mail; nothing restricts the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. Section 2(a) affirmatively preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or license competing software and services (subject only to TrueLink's IP and our confidentiality obligations), which exceeds the playbook's preferred position. The "ordinary course of business" wording in Section 2(a) defines the scope of the licence granted to us rather than restricting our other activities. The only non-competition reference (Section 8(d)) makes TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data subject to a separate Non-Competition Agreement, i.e. a limitation on the vendor, which is acceptable; we should nonetheless review that separate agreement to confirm it imposes no restraint on us. No redline required.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made our termination right explicit: Client may terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a refund of prepaid fees and no penalty, and TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right. We also lengthened TrueLink's non-renewal notice to 90 days so we have time to migrate hosting (Section 13 already requires us to arrange a new environment within 60 days), leaving our own 30-day non-renewal notice unchanged.

ops.newText: 14. TERMINATION. Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to TrueLink, without penalty or early termination fee, in which case TrueLink shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services through the effective date of termination. TrueLink shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the then-current term.

ops.oldText: unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year

proposal.summary: Add express Client termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with prepaid-fee refund; bar TrueLink mid-term convenience termination; extend TrueLink's non-renewal notice to 90 days.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Section 14 only implies a Client exit (services continue "until the last day of the month following" our notice) rather than granting an express termination-for-convenience right, sets an uncertain notice period of up to ~60 days, and provides no refund of prepaid fees. Nothing states that TrueLink may not walk away mid-term, and Section 13 lets TrueLink exit at renewal on only 30 days' notice, which is below the playbook floor of 90 days and inconsistent with the 60-day migration window Section 13 imposes on us. Redline makes our 30-day convenience right and prepaid-fee refund explicit, bars TrueLink's mid-term convenience termination, and extends TrueLink's non-renewal notice to 90 days while preserving our 30-day non-renewal notice.

quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged
rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right exercisable by TrueLink against Client. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books" and "monitor" return nothing, and the sections where such rights are usually tucked away are clean: § 5–6 (Compensation/Documentation) runs in our favour, giving Client the right to supporting documentation and to contest charges rather than giving TrueLink reconciliation audit rights; § 8 (Client covenants) imposes only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties with no verification right; § 10 (Confidentiality) contains no inspection mechanic. The only related items are TrueLink's right under § 8(f) to implement technical mechanisms on its own hosted Interface to prevent spamming/illegal use, and Client's Y2K-related obligation in § 9 to provide reasonable access for TrueLink's own repairs at TrueLink's cost — neither is a usage audit nor grants access to Client systems or records. With no audit right binding us, there is no exposure on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access, so the playbook position is satisfied and no redline is needed.

quote: 26. APPLICABLE LAW. This Agreement shall be governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of California (without respect to principles of conflicts of law).
rationale: Sections 26 and 27 select California law with exclusive venue in the state or federal courts of San Luis Obispo County, California, and each party consents to that jurisdiction. California law and California courts are within the playbook's accepted list (fallback position), and there is no arbitration provision anywhere in the agreement (searches for "arbitration" return no results), so no foreign arbitral seat or foreign exclusive venue is imposed. The clause is mutual and does not reach the walk-away position, so we accept it as drafted rather than spending negotiating capital to move to the preferred New York forum.

quote: TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.
rationale: The sole most-favoured-nation style provision (Section 6, in the COMPENSATION section) runs in our favour: TrueLink undertakes that Hosting Services rates will not exceed those charged to any other party, coupled with a one-year price freeze. Nothing in the compensation, license, or client covenant provisions obliges Mortgage Logic.com to extend TrueLink terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers. Consistent with the rule's direction test, a Vendor-granted MFN is welcome and is not redlined.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the minimum monthly Hosting Services and Support Services fee floor so that we pay only for services we actually request, consistent with our position against take-or-pay commitments, and removed the related carve-outs so all charges remain subject to supporting documentation and dispute rights. If TrueLink needs a floor, we can accept one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued-up rather than penalised.

ops.oldText: hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).

ops.newText: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged and will be entitled to contest any charge, provided that Client timely pays all contested amounts.
ops.oldText: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4), provided that Client timely pays all contested amounts.

proposal.summary: Delete the minimum monthly Hosting/Support fee floor and the related carve-outs from Client's documentation and dispute rights

quote: a. Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
rationale: Section 5(a) imposes a minimum monthly fee floor on Client for both Hosting and Support Services regardless of usage, i.e. a take-or-pay commitment, and Section 6 expressly strips Client of documentation and dispute rights for those minimum fees. The term auto-renews for successive one-year periods (Section 13), so the floor recurs indefinitely, and the amounts are left blank. Client's at-will exit under Section 14 (effective the last day of the month following notice) mitigates but does not remove the commitment, and there is no true-up mechanism. We therefore delete the minimum and the related carve-outs to reach the preferred position (pay for usage/ordered services only), offering the 12-month, notice-reducible, trued-up floor as fallback.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: d. Use of Credit Data during the term of this Agreement. Client hereby grants to TrueLink the nonexclusive worldwide right and license to use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit, upload, display, copy and store Credit Data subject to the limitations set forth in and in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire or employee-inducement covenant binding Client (Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.). Targeted searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel" and "recruit" return only an unrelated anti-spam provision (§ 7 Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail) and references to employees in the access-restriction (§ 8(c)) and indemnity (§ 12) provisions. The Client covenants section (§ 8) and the confidentiality section (§ 10) — the usual homes for such covenants — impose no hiring or solicitation restrictions on Client. The only restrictive-covenant reference is § 8(d)'s cross-reference to a separate Non-Competition Agreement, which limits use of Credit Data and does not incorporate any employee non-solicit into this Agreement. This matches our preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so no redline is required; if TrueLink later proposes one, we would hold to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 30-day non-renewal window and one-year renewal term work for us, but we have added a 60-day renewal reminder from TrueLink and a cap on renewal-term fee increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, consistent with our position that renewals be predictably priced and easy to exit. If helpful, we can accept a flat 5% cap as a fallback.

ops.newText: no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year. TrueLink will notify Client in writing of each upcoming renewal no later than sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term. Fees for any renewal term will not increase by more than the lesser of (i) the percentage increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%), in each case measured against the fees in effect during the immediately preceding term.

proposal.summary: Add vendor renewal reminder (60 days) and cap renewal price increases at lesser of CPI and 3%

quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
rationale: Section 13 (p0078) provides automatic renewal for successive one-year terms with a mutual 30-day non-renewal notice window, which already meets the preferred renewal term length (12 months) and opt-out window (30 days). However, two elements of the preferred position are absent: there is no vendor reminder ahead of renewal, and there is no cap on renewal-term price increases — the only pricing protection is the one-year fee freeze in Section 6 (p0047), which expires before the first renewal, leaving uplift uncapped thereafter. Redline adds a 60-day TrueLink renewal reminder and caps renewal fee increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with a 5% flat cap offered as fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14 ends the Hosting and Support Services but says nothing about getting our hosted data back or help moving off the Interface, and Section 13 puts the entire burden of re-hosting on us. We have added our standard exit provision: up to six months of transition assistance at TrueLink's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day data export and deletion certification stay.

ops.text: Transition Assistance and Return of Client Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (i) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Web Site and Client Data to Client or its designee; (ii) within thirty (30) days of Client's request, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other data and information of Client or its customers stored in or processed through the Interface or the Web Site (collectively, "Client Data") in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete all Client Data from its systems and backups, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law, and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and certified deletion obligations into Section 14 (Termination).

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: This is a hosting and licensing agreement under which TrueLink stores the Web Site, Client Content and Credit Data on its own servers (Sections 3(a), 3(f), 8(d)), yet neither the termination provisions (Sections 13 and 14) nor the confidentiality provisions (Section 10) require TrueLink to return or export our data, to delete it after exit, or to assist with migration. Section 13 in fact places the entire exit burden on us ("Client is responsible for arranging for a new hosting environment within 60 days"). The playbook preferred position requires up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter, so the absence is a deviation warranting insertion. The new subsection is added in Section 14, which survives termination under Section 24.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 gives us only a Y2K warranty, so TrueLink stands behind nothing about how the Interface and Hosting/Support Services actually perform; we have added our standard performance and conformance warranty (12 months for software, 90 days for services), compliance with laws, no malicious code, and a repair/replace/refund remedy. If TrueLink cannot accept the 12-month software period, we can fall back to 90 days for software and 30 days for services with the same remedies.

ops.text: TrueLink further represents and warrants that (a) the Hosting Services and Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (b) for a period of twelve (12) months following delivery, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation and specifications, and for a period of ninety (90) days following performance, the Hosting Services and Support Services will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement; (c) TrueLink will comply in all material respects with laws applicable to its performance under this Agreement; and (d) the Interface and all related software will be free of viruses, worms, Trojan horses and any other malicious code. proposal.summary: Add a TrueLink performance/conformance warranty with repair-replace-refund remedy in Section 9

quote: 9. TRUELINK WARRANTIES. TrueLink represents and warrants that the Interface and all related software (i) is designed to be used before, on and after January l, 2000;
rationale: Section 9 is the only TrueLink warranty and is limited to Y2K date processing; there is no warranty that the Interface, related software or the Hosting/Support Services will be performed in a workmanlike manner or conform to documentation, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair/replace/refund remedy. Section 8 contains Client-side warranties only, and p0042 expressly disclaims any warranty as to transmitted data. The disclaimer at p0076 is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does not swallow an added express warranty, but with no express performance warranty the effect is close to AS IS. Under the playbook this missing express warranty is a deviation requiring insertion of the preferred 12-month software / 90-day services conformance warranty with a real remedy.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance provision even though TrueLink hosts our Web Site and handles Client Content and Credit Data, so we have added our standard coverages (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation) with certificates on request. If USD 5M cyber is not available, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M.

ops.text: 31. INSURANCE. TrueLink shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering TrueLink's hosting, processing, storage and transmission of Client Content, Credit Data and other Client data; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. TrueLink shall provide Client with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 31 requiring TrueLink to carry CGL, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation insurance and to provide certificates on request.

quote: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. TrueLink will be excused from delays in performing or from failing to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent the delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control or TrueLink.
rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance provision (search for "insurance" returns nothing; the general provisions run from Section 15 through Section 30 with no coverage requirement), even though TrueLink hosts our Web Site and processes Client Content and Credit Data (consumer credit information). Playbook requires standard vendor coverages, including E&O and cyber/privacy, for vendors touching Customer Data. Inserted a new Section 31 after the final general provision (Force Majeure, p0097) requiring CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request; fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M offered in the comment.
